doc.title: Håkan Rydin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Glasgow, Scotland, July 27, 2016

title: The Glasgow rhythm section and the communication of playing
summary: The musicians met an hour and a half before the gig; Rydin explains the direct communication of playing music.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: I was trying to determine if the fellas you were playing with — how long you’ve been playing with them.
Yes that’s a very — we met one and a half hours before and we had a 30 minute rehearsal. But I sent the music to them by email in advance.
They did a good job. And at one point, I can’t recall the song, but you were playing and you looked up at the bass player and he was looking at you —
And the whole band went up a step.

Yes, those amazing moments. I mean that’s why it’s so nice to play music, isn’t it, because it’s another kind of communication. It’s very direct. [claps] I mean it’s like that. I mean we can talk and we can communicate pretty good I hope, but playing is another level, not necessarily higher, but another level of communication. Very direct, very honest in a way. I mean it’s there. It should be there.
